What's new in 2.36.0

Two people can now work one herd at the same time. Name the same session on the same server and you are both looking at the same panes and the same agents — in your own tabs, at once, with your own SSH connection.

Share a herd ⌃⌥.

  • A Session field on every server. Put the same name in it on two Macs — team, say — and both of you are clients of the same herd on that machine. Leave it blank and nothing changes: that's the server's own herd, exactly as before.
  • Different tabs at the same time. Clicking a pane used to move the other person's view, because a herd has one focused pane and Dax was setting it on every click. Your selection is yours now — you can be in one tab while they're in another, both live.
  • You can see who else is there. Their name sits beside the machine's name in the switcher, and a pane somebody is driving says so.
  • One driver per terminal, and it's deliberate. Open a pane your teammate is typing in and you get a live view of it rather than taking their keyboard out from under them. Take Control moves it to you, on purpose, when you want it.
  • Nobody is the host. The herd lives on the server, so whoever closes their laptop, the agents keep working and the other person keeps watching.

What it needs

  • The same server and the same account on it, with each person's SSH key added — Dax doesn't need anything else, and nothing is relayed through us.
  • Simultaneous work means a pane each. Two people typing into one terminal is a race whatever the app does about it.

Also in this release

  • Adding an agent lands where you asked. A new agent could appear beside the wrong pane, in the wrong project — Dax was naming the pane to split with the wrong field, so herdr split whatever was focused instead.
  • Signed, notarized, universal (Apple Silicon & Intel), macOS 14+.
